idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api was failing health checks after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate ~18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Remediation: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0, the most recent version that was healthy in production, across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Note: the initial rollback attempt partially applied (us-east only) due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the rollback. Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator error before attempting redeploy.

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what happened:

**Rollback completed**
- checkout-api was running v2.3.1 (unhealthy, ~18% error rate) across us-east, us-west, and eu-west.
- Identified **v2.3.0** as the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- The first rollback attempt partially applied (us-east only) due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the rollout to all three regions.
- Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, **service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%**.

**Incident opened**
- A SEV2 incident was opened for checkout-api documenting the v2.3.1 health-check failures and the rollback to v2.3.0; the on-call engineer was paged.

**One caveat:** the initial incident-creation request timed out but had actually succeeded on the backend (INC-0001). My retry with a fresh idempotency key created a second, identical incident (INC-0002), so there is now a duplicate. I don't have a tool to close incidents, so someone should close one of the duplicates (suggest keeping INC-0001 as the canonical record) and the follow-up items noted in the incident: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator error before any redeploy attempt.

The incident should be created after rollback so I can describe what I did. Rollback call first; incident depends on its outcome. Actually I can do them sequentially: rollback, then create incident.

transcript.content: Only us-east rolled back; the orchestrator halted. I'll retry the rollback to complete all regions.
Rollback completed successfully — service is healthy again. Now I'll open the SEV2 incident.
